rationale: The standard requires students to identify four story-crafting techniques: characters, setting, major events, and dialogue. Characters: students identify and discuss the boy and the sun as characters ("Discuss with a partner what the boy and sun are doing using the frame: In the end, the boy is _____. The sun is _____."). Major events: students act out ending events via the Role-Play protocol for pages 21–26 and complete a response sheet writing/drawing about ending events ("At the end …"). Setting is only partially addressed — students answer time/place questions ("Where is the sun at sunset?") but the teacher supplies most of the explicit setting identification, and the lesson never frames setting as a story technique for students to identify. Dialogue is not addressed: no activity asks students to identify or discuss dialogue as a technique used in the story. Because two clauses are met, one is partially met, and one is not met, the alignment is partial.
